validity.recommendation: review status - no independent evidence of the project since October 2018
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and independently documented. Delmarva Pipeline Company, a subsidiary of Baltimore-based H4 Capital Partners LLC, proposed a 180-190 mile natural gas pipeline from Rising Sun, Md. down the Delmarva peninsula to Accomack County, Va., ran an open season from August to October 2017 (Bay Journal), presented the plan to Eastern Shore legislators in January 2018 (WBOC), and by April 2018 was listed in P&GJ's planned-projects table as 'preparing to file with FERC'. Five independent publishers name the line: the trade press (P&GJ), regional agricultural press (Farm Progress), two local newspapers (Cecil Whig, Dorchester Star / myeasternshoremd), a regional environmental newsroom (Bay Journal) and an advocacy analyst with its own route mapping (FracTracker, which digitised the corridor and counted 172 stream and 579 wetland crossings). CLASSIFICATION: correct - an interstate gas transmission trunk, not a gathering or distribution line; it would have interconnected to the Transco system in Pennsylvania/Cecil County. DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate of anything on the 46-row roster; and explicitly NOT the Eastern Shore Natural Gas / Chesapeake Utilities Del-Mar Energy Pathway, a separate, smaller, actually-built Delmarva expansion that reached service in 2021 - Bay Journal and myeasternshoremd both state ESNG 'is not affiliated with Delmarva Pipeline Company'. Do not let later 'Delmarva' gas-pipeline coverage (the 2021 Maryland approval story) be read onto this row. CAVEAT: the independent record stops dead in October 2018. No FERC application under Delmarva Pipeline Company was ever located, and no publisher has covered the project since; see status_reviews. RULE-1 REPAIR 2026-09-14: the wiki ref this record previously carried was removed under standing rule 1 (never cite GEM) and replaced with the five independent sources above.

The only source anywhere giving a later year is offshore-technology.com's GlobalData market-data profile ('expected to commence operations in 2025'), which is also wrong on diameter (26 inches vs the sourced 8 and 24) and on the end state (it says the line starts and ends in Maryland), so it was not used. The Start [ref] fill stages 2021 with three independent refs. status_reviews.researcher_notes: RULE-1 REPAIR 2026-09-14: the prose of this review previously rested on the GEM wiki page and has been rewritten off independent sources; the inference itself correctly carries no ref (standing rule 2). Hunted for evidence newer than the sheet's LastUpdated (2024-08-24) and found NONE: the last independent coverage of this project anywhere is Bay Journal, 24 October 2018 (evidence_date 2018-10). At that point the project was live - P&GJ's April-2018 entry reads 'Status: Project is preparing to file with FERC' and Bay Journal reported Sanders saying H4 'plans to file an application this fall' with FERC. No such FERC application was ever located, no FERC docket for Delmarva Pipeline Company surfaced, no Maryland PSC or Virginia SCC proceeding was found, and no publisher has written about the line in eight years. Searched: all 9 harvested citations; open-web on 'Delmarva Pipeline' + shelved/abandoned/stalled/cancelled/FERC/withdrawn for 2019-2026; 'H4 Capital Partners' and 'Delmarva Pipeline Company' by name; FERC eLibrary; Maryland and Delaware PSC document stores; the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects long table (no Delmarva record in any of the 28 releases). DISAMBIGUATION that matters here: the Delmarva gas pipeline that DID get built and reached service in 2021 is Chesapeake Utilities / Eastern Shore Natural Gas's Del-Mar Energy Pathway, a separate company explicitly 'not affiliated with Delmarva Pipeline Company' - it is not this row and must not be read as a revival. Verdict stale under the dormancy rule: shelved with no progress >= 4y -> cancelled with ShelvedCancelledType = inferred. CancelledYear is set to 2022 rather than 2024 - dormancy runs from the last evidence (Oct 2018), so the 4-year threshold was crossed in 2022; the earlier 2024 value was tied to the unsourced 2024 start year, which this pass corrected to 2021 (see validity spec concern).
